principles.statement: Increasing per-thread NVMe queue depth from 8 to 64 on the batch_lookup path improves cold-lookup throughput by ~56% (3.63 → 5.99 GB/s) on dual Gen4 NVMe SSDs with 4 MiB sequential reads at 128 KiB chunks. This is the single largest performance lever for the batch path, exceeding the previous 21% estimate which was based on the single-object path only.
principles.regime: Batch cold lookups with 2 NVMe Gen4 SSDs, 128 KiB chunks, 4 MiB objects, 16 objects per batch. Single-client, 2 threads per drive (MAX_QUEUES_PER_DRIVE=2).
principles.mechanism: The batch_lookup path divides queue_depth_budget by num_queues to set per-thread NVMe command depth. At QD8 (budget=16, 2 threads), only 25% of a 4 MiB object's 32 chunks are in flight simultaneously. At QD64, all 32 chunks for 2 objects can be submitted before waiting for completions, saturating the NVMe controller's internal command scheduler. The actor selects the depth-64 hardware queue pair instead of depth-16, enabling the device's multi-die parallelism.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to batch path with 2+ drives. Single-drive configurations at aggregate QD128+ trigger ENOMEM (see RP-3 update). Maximum benefit already captured at QD64; going higher provides no additional gain.

principles.statement: Increasing NVMe chunk size from 128 KiB to 512 KiB reduces cold-lookup throughput by ~5% because fewer pipeline segments reduce overlap opportunity in the sliding-window pipeline.
principles.regime: 4 MiB objects, QD16, pipelined sliding-window transfer, single Gen4 NVMe drive
principles.mechanism: With 512 KiB chunks, a 4 MiB object has only 8 segments. The sliding-window pipeline can only keep min(QD, num_segments) operations in-flight. At 8 segments, the pipeline drains too quickly — there are not enough independent operations to fully overlap NVMe reads with GPU DMA copies. At 128 KiB (32 segments), the pipeline maintains steady-state overlap throughout the transfer. The per-command overhead reduction from fewer commands is smaller than the parallelism loss.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to 4 MiB objects specifically. For much larger objects (tens of MiB+), larger chunks might become beneficial since segment count would remain high. May not apply to purely sequential non-overlapped reads where per-command overhead dominates.

principles.statement: Aggregate NVMe queue depth above ~96-128 per single controller causes sporadic SPDK submission failures (ENOMEM/rc=-12) even at 128 KiB chunk sizes. The previous threshold observation (512 KiB + QD64) was a special case of a more general resource exhaustion boundary that depends on total concurrent commands, not just per-command size.
principles.regime: Single NVMe Gen4 controller with 4 threads × QD32 = aggregate QD128, 128 KiB chunks, 16 objects per batch.
principles.mechanism: The NVMe controller's scatter-gather entry pool or internal request tracker is finite. With 4 threads each submitting QD32 commands (each requiring scatter-gather entries for 128 KiB), the total pending commands (128) exhaust resources during burst submission windows where all 4 threads submit simultaneously. The SPDK queue pair depth-256 is sufficient in queue slots but the underlying NVMe controller firmware rejects commands when internal resources are full.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to single-controller configurations. With 2 drives (8 objects each, 2 threads each, QD64 per thread = 128 aggregate per drive), the same aggregate QD works fine — the hardware limit appears to be per-controller, and the actual boundary may be higher when commands don't arrive in a burst.

principles.statement: Removing or relaxing periodic GPU stream synchronization (every 16 H2D copies) has no measurable throughput impact at low NVMe queue depths (QD16) because the GPU sync stall (~167 us) is not the pipeline bottleneck when the NVMe device is already underutilized with only 16 in-flight commands.
principles.regime: QD16, 2 CUDA streams, 128 KiB chunks, 4 MiB objects (32 chunks), single-client, 2x Gen4 NVMe drives
principles.mechanism: At QD16, the sliding window can have at most 16 NVMe reads in flight. With 32 chunks per 4 MiB object, the sync fires once at stream_idx=16 (mid-object). However, removing this sync yields 3.76 GB/s vs baseline 3.78 GB/s — no improvement. The NVMe device's internal parallelism is already constrained by the shallow queue (only 16 commands visible to the drive's scheduler), so the ~167 us GPU stall doesn't create a meaningful pipeline bubble — the NVMe completions simply aren't arriving fast enough to be starved.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to QD<=16 configurations. At higher queue depths (QD64), the GPU sync overhead may become relatively more significant, though iter-2 h-ablation showed only marginal (+1.3%) benefit from sync removal on top of QD64+4 streams.

principles.statement: At QD64 + 4 CUDA streams, removing the periodic GPU sync provides at most marginal throughput improvement (~1.3%, within measurement noise), confirming that NVMe queue depth and stream parallelism are the dominant factors for cold-lookup throughput, not GPU synchronization overhead.
principles.regime: QD64, 4 CUDA streams, 128 KiB chunks, 4 MiB objects, single-client, 2x Gen4 NVMe drives, ~4.5 GB/s throughput
principles.mechanism: Iteration 1 achieved 4.53 GB/s with QD64+4 streams WITH the periodic sync. Iteration 2 h-ablation achieves 4.59 GB/s with the same config MINUS the sync — a delta of only +1.3% (0.06 GB/s). At QD64, the deeper NVMe queue ensures completions arrive fast enough to keep the pipeline busy even during a brief GPU sync stall. The sync at 16 copies takes ~167 us, during which the 64-deep NVMe queue still has ample completions buffered. Removing it yields minimal benefit because the NVMe queue never drains to empty during the stall.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to the 4.5 GB/s throughput regime on 2x Gen4 NVMe + A30 GPU. At higher drive counts or near-saturation throughput, the sync overhead might become relatively more significant. The sync can be safely removed (no correctness impact) but the performance benefit is negligible.

principles.statement: Increasing thread count from 2 to 4 per drive (MAX_QUEUES_PER_DRIVE) while holding total aggregate queue depth constant at 128 reduces throughput by ~7% compared to 2 threads with deeper per-thread queues, due to NVMe actor poll-loop contention.
principles.regime: Batch cold lookups with 2 NVMe Gen4 SSDs, 128 KiB chunks, 4 MiB objects, 16 objects per batch. Comparing 4×QD32 vs 2×QD64 at same aggregate depth.
principles.mechanism: The NVMe block device actor runs a single-threaded poll loop (actor.rs) that multiplexes all client channels. With 4 threads, the actor processes 4 command channels and 4 completion channels vs 2, adding per-iteration overhead to the poll loop. Additionally, 4 threads create/destroy 4 CUDA streams each (vs 2), adding ~50% more GPU API overhead per batch. The NVMe controller receives the same aggregate QD128 in both cases, so device-side parallelism is identical — the difference is purely software overhead.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies when the NVMe actor is the multiplexing bottleneck. If the actor were multi-threaded or if hardware queue pairs were used directly (bypassing the actor), the thread count penalty might disappear. The 7% penalty may also diminish with larger objects (more chunks) where per-thread pipeline latency hiding becomes more valuable.

principles.statement: Expanding CUDA streams from 2 to 4 provides no measurable throughput benefit for batch cold lookups at 5-6 GB/s aggregate throughput, confirming that GPU DMA bandwidth is not the bottleneck at these throughput levels.
principles.regime: Batch cold lookups at 5-6 GB/s aggregate, PCIe Gen4 x16 GPU, 128 KiB H2D copies.
principles.mechanism: PCIe Gen4 x16 provides ~25 GB/s unidirectional bandwidth. At 6 GB/s aggregate throughput, the GPU DMA path is only 24% utilized. Two CUDA streams already provide sufficient H2D copy overlap since individual DMA copies (128 KiB) complete in ~5 us while NVMe reads take ~30 us — the GPU is always waiting for NVMe, not the reverse. Additional streams add creation/destruction overhead without enabling any additional overlap.
principles.applicability_bounds: May change if throughput exceeds ~12 GB/s (48% PCIe utilization) or if multiple clients drive concurrent DMA copies that could contend on the GPU's DMA engines. Also may change with larger chunk sizes where individual DMA latency matters more.
